# Copilot instructions for aidlc-workflows

AI-DLC (AI-Driven Development Life Cycle) is a methodology for guiding AI coding
agents through structured software development workflows. This repository contains
the core workflow rules, detailed phase-specific rules, and a Python evaluator
framework. It is **content-first** — almost everything here is Markdown, not code.

The distributable product is the `aidlc-rules/` directory, which is zipped and
published via GitHub Releases.

> This file is the always-on, repository-wide context for GitHub Copilot. See
> [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for the fuller contributor guide (this file is a
> concise subset that also helps Copilot surfaces that do not read `AGENTS.md`,
> such as basic github.com Chat and code review).

## Repository layout

- `aidlc-rules/aws-aidlc-rules/core-workflow.md` — the single workflow entry point.
- `aidlc-rules/aws-aidlc-rule-details/` — detailed rules loaded on demand
  (`common/`, `inception/`, `construction/`, `extensions/`, `operations/`).
- `scripts/aidlc-evaluator/` — Python evaluation framework (uv-managed, pytest).
- `docs/` — human-facing guides (see the map below).
- `.github/` — CI/CD workflows, issue/PR templates, and these instruction files.

## Which docs to read by task type

- CI/CD, workflows, or releases → `docs/ADMINISTRATIVE_GUIDE.md`,
  `docs/DEVELOPERS_GUIDE.md`.
- `aidlc-rules/` content → `docs/WORKING-WITH-AIDLC.md`,
  `docs/GENERATED_DOCS_REFERENCE.md`.
- Vision or technical-environment inputs → `docs/writing-inputs/`.

## Commands

```bash
# Lint all Markdown (run before committing)
npx markdownlint-cli2 "**/*.md"
npx markdownlint-cli2 --fix "**/*.md"

# Evaluator tests (from scripts/aidlc-evaluator/)
uv run pytest
uv run pytest --cov --cov-report=term-missing
```

## Code style

- All content is Markdown — follow `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`.
- MD040 (fenced code language) and MD060 (aligned table pipes) are enforced —
  always add a language to code fences and keep table columns aligned.
- MD013, MD033, MD024, and MD036 are intentionally disabled.
- Commit messages follow [conventional commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
  (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`).

## Pull request rules

- PR titles must follow conventional commits.
- Use the structure from `.github/pull_request_template.md`.
- The PR body **must** end with this contributor statement (CI enforces it):

  > By submitting this pull request, I confirm that you can use, modify, copy,
  > and redistribute this contribution, under the terms of the
  > [project license](https://github.com/awslabs/aidlc-workflows/blob/main/LICENSE).

## Security scanners

Six scanners run on push to `main`, on every PR, and daily (Bandit, Semgrep,
Grype, Gitleaks, Checkov, ClamAV). All HIGH/CRITICAL findings must be remediated
or have documented risk acceptance before merge. Inline suppressions:

- Bandit: `# nosec BXXX — justification`
- Semgrep: `# nosemgrep: rule-id — justification`
- Checkov: `# checkov:skip=CKV_ID:justification`

## Important constraints

- The folder names `aws-aidlc-rules/` and `aws-aidlc-rule-details/` are part of
  the public contract — never rename, move, or reorganize them.
- Do not duplicate content across rules — put shared guidance in `common/` and
  reference it.
- Keep the core methodology IDE/agent/model agnostic.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is auto-generated by git-cliff — never edit it by hand.
- Report security issues via
  [AWS vulnerability reporting](http://aws.amazon.com/security/vulnerability-reporting/),
  not public GitHub issues.
